lines.text: Do you know how Neuralink works? A chip in the brain that lets people move a cursor just by thinking about it.
The implant is about the size of a coin. It replaces a small circle of skull, and sits hidden under the skin.
From it, sixty four threads, each far thinner than a human hair, reach into the brain, carrying one thousand and twenty four electrodes.
They're too fine for human hands. So a surgical robot inserts them, steering around blood vessels.
Neurons talk in tiny electrical spikes. When you even imagine moving your hand, a pattern of spikes fires in the part of the brain that controls movement.
The electrodes pick up those spikes, and software learns which pattern means left, right, or click.
The signals go to a computer over Bluetooth. And the battery charges wirelessly, right through the skin.
By September twenty twenty five, twelve people with paralysis had one, using it to play games and browse the web with their thoughts.
It's not mind reading. It's movement decoding. For now.
